title: Python SDK: ergonomic streaming chat completions with event-driven handlers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship an ergonomically pleasant Python SDK surface for streaming chat completions that exposes event-driven handlers (token, delta, structured event, done, error) and composes cleanly with retries and cancellation. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, docs, and example apps for the new streaming API pattern.

Background: Current Python SDK exposes low-level iterators for streaming responses which forces users to write boilerplate parsing and brittle state machines. We want higher-level primitives that are:
- Easy to integrate with async/await code and sync code via helpers.
- Support pluggable backoff/retry on transient connection errors while preserving at-least-once or exactly-once semantics as appropriate.
- Emit well-typed event objects (as Python dataclasses) to enable typed handler callbacks and simplified testing.
- Keep compatibility shim for existing iterator-based codepaths.

Scope: Implement streaming ChatCompletion client helpers + event classes + example patterns. Provide:
1) ChatStream class with async iterator and callback registration (.on_token, .on_delta, .on_event, .on_done, .on_error).
2) A high-level convenience function `stream_chat` that accepts either async callbacks or returns an async iterator.
3) Retry wrapper that can be enabled per-call with configurable max_retries, backoff_strategy, and idempotency_mode.
4) Cancellation support via asyncio.CancelledError propagation and context manager for sync usage.
5) Documentation page, example notebooks, and a small demo app (streaming chat + live UI).

Non-goals: We will not change server-side event envelope formats; we adapt to current server schema. We will not implement full public typed dataclasses for every possible structured event in this ticket—cover common events and an extensible base event.
acceptance_criteria: Public API provides ChatStream with .on_* callback registration and async iterator compat
stream_chat convenience function available in both sync and async flavors
Retries can be toggled per-call, with sensible defaults (3 attempts, jittered exponential) and preserves previously yielded tokens when safe
Unit and integration tests covering: normal streaming, server disconnect + retry, cancellation, and structured event parsing
Example notebook added to docs/streaming_chat.ipynb and example app in examples/streaming_chat_demo.py
Benchmark: CPU overhead of wrapper <5% compared to raw iterator for typical 512-token stream
Docs include migration guide from raw iterator to new handlers
notes: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting — agreed on event types and names: TokenEvent, DeltaEvent, StructuredEvent, DoneEvent, ErrorEvent.
2026-03-11: Prototype of ChatStream with .on_token completed by @miguel. Basic async iterator wrapper works.
2026-03-12: Design decision: Use dataclasses for events rather than Pydantic to keep dependency surface small.
2026-03-13: UX review with DX: prefer explicit `await stream.wait()` for finalization instead of implicit close in iterator to avoid silent swallow of errors.
2026-03-14: PR #1482 opened (WIP) with implementation and unit tests. Initial review requested from @sophia and @omar.
Trade-offs: Higher-level API will add ~70 LOC wrapper. We avoid bundling a full reactive library to keep SDK light.
Open question: default retry idempotency semantics for chat streams — currently using "request-idempotency" header from server to influence retries if present.
example_usage:
# Async usage with callbacks
from redwood import PythonClient
from redwood.streaming import ChatStream, TokenEvent, DoneEvent

client = PythonClient(api_key=... )

async def run():
    stream = await client.chat.stream_chat(model="gpt-open-7b", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Write a haiku about servers"}], retry={"max_retries":3})

    # register callbacks
    stream.on_token(lambda ev: print(ev.text))
    stream.on_event(lambda ev: print(f"STRUCTURED: {ev.type} {ev.payload}"))
    stream.on_done(lambda ev: print('done', ev.summary))

    # await completion (also supports async for token in stream:)
    await stream.wait()

# Sync convenience helper
from redwood import sync_client

def sync_example():
    with sync_client.chat.stream_chat_sync(... ) as stream:
        for token_event in stream:
            print(token_event.text)

# Iterator compatibility
async for event in client.chat.stream_chat(...):
    if event.kind == 'token':
        process(event.text)
decisions: Use dataclasses for event objects to minimize deps and maximize typing support
Provide both callback registration and async iterator compatibility to support different user patterns
Retry default: 3 attempts with jittered exponential backoff; retries only on transport errors and 5xx; not on application-level structured events unless server indicates safe replay
Keep backward-compatible iterator yield values: yield Event objects with .kind field so older code can adapt gradually
tests: unit/test_stream_handlers.py: handler registration, event ordering, cancellation
integration/test_stream_retry.py: simulate TCP resets and assert retry preserves or replays tokens according to idempotency flag
e2e/examples/streaming_chat_demo_test.py: launch example app and validate UI receives tokens
load/benchmark_stream_wrapper.py: microbench to measure wrapper overhead

Add example showing how to attach a deterministic retry policy that resumes from last acknowledged token when server provides offset tokens
Publish docs and release notes for python-sdk-2.4.0 once PR merged
